article.title: Claros Technologies Raises $55 Million Series B to Scale 'Forever Chemical' Destruction Technology
article.summary: The Minneapolis startup will expand its ClarosTechUV PFAS destruction system after demonstrating over 99.99% removal in industrial and groundwater tests.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Claros Technologies, a Minneapolis-based company that destroys PFAS — the class of synthetic compounds known as "forever chemicals" — has closed a $55 million Series B financing round, according to [Claros's press release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/claros-technologies-raises-55-million-series-b-financing-to-accelerate-global-commercialization-of-pfas-destruction-technology-302835890.html) and independently confirmed by [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/07/28/venture-capital-startup-funding-roundup-july-28-2026-battery-ventures-bessemer-gradient-team8-y-combinator-more/). The round, which is inclusive of the company's previously announced convertible note financing, will fund global commercialization of its ClarosTechUV destruction system and expansion of its ClarosLabs analytical testing division.

## What We Know

The Series B was led by [Treehouse Family Capital LLC](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/claros-technologies-raises-55-million-series-b-financing-to-accelerate-global-commercialization-of-pfas-destruction-technology-302835890.html), with participation from Daikin America, Veralto, Bush Foundation, Nord Asset Management, and Saint Paul & Minnesota Foundation, alongside existing investors — a lineup confirmed identically by [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/07/28/venture-capital-startup-funding-roundup-july-28-2026-battery-ventures-bessemer-gradient-team8-y-combinator-more/).

Claros, founded in 2018, operates two divisions: ClarosTech, which builds permanent PFAS destruction systems, and ClarosLabs, an [ISO/IEC 17025:2017 accredited](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/claros-technologies-raises-55-million-series-b-financing-to-accelerate-global-commercialization-of-pfas-destruction-technology-302835890.html) analytical-testing operation. The company points to two recent technical demonstrations as evidence its process works at commercial scale. In December 2025, a partnership with Daikin America achieved [greater than 99.99% destruction](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/claros-technologies-raises-55-million-series-b-financing-to-accelerate-global-commercialization-of-pfas-destruction-technology-302835890.html) of long-, short-, and ultra-short chain PFAS compounds in an industrial process water demonstration. In April 2026, the company demonstrated [≥99.99% destruction](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/claros-technologies-raises-55-million-series-b-financing-to-accelerate-global-commercialization-of-pfas-destruction-technology-302835890.html) of targeted PFAS in groundwater remediation, using concentrate derived from approximately one million gallons of groundwater.

Michelle Bellanca, Claros's chief executive officer and co-founder, said the company has "[crossed the threshold from breakthrough technology to successful commercial reality](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/claros-technologies-raises-55-million-series-b-financing-to-accelerate-global-commercialization-of-pfas-destruction-technology-302835890.html)" over the past year — a line she is quoted using in both the company's release and [Tech Startups's](https://techstartups.com/2026/07/28/venture-capital-startup-funding-roundup-july-28-2026-battery-ventures-bessemer-gradient-team8-y-combinator-more/) coverage. [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/07/28/venture-capital-startup-funding-roundup-july-28-2026-battery-ventures-bessemer-gradient-team8-y-combinator-more/) also quotes her saying the demonstrations prove permanent destruction operates "reliably, efficiently and cost-effectively at commercial scale." Jack Cogen, manager of lead investor Treehouse Family Capital, said in the [company's release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/claros-technologies-raises-55-million-series-b-financing-to-accelerate-global-commercialization-of-pfas-destruction-technology-302835890.html) that "the most exciting technology companies eventually reach an inflection point where the question is no longer whether the technology works, but how quickly it can be deployed at scale."

According to [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/07/28/venture-capital-startup-funding-roundup-july-28-2026-battery-ventures-bessemer-gradient-team8-y-combinator-more/), the new funding will support commercial deployments across North America, Europe, and Asia, and the company frames its technology as relevant to industries — including semiconductor manufacturing, aerospace, pharmaceuticals, and healthcare — that continue to rely on PFAS for specific applications even as pressure builds to remediate contamination from past use.

The raise lands amid tightening PFAS regulation on both sides of the Atlantic: [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/07/28/venture-capital-startup-funding-roundup-july-28-2026-battery-ventures-bessemer-gradient-team8-y-combinator-more/) notes that Europe is advancing broad restrictions under proposed REACH Regulation frameworks while U.S. federal and state agencies expand drinking-water standards and remediation programs, both dynamics the outlet ties to growing demand for destruction and analytical services like Claros's.

Claros's approach is one of several PFAS-remediation technologies to draw investment and attention this year; The Machine Herald has [previously reported](/article/2026-04/09-flinders-universitys-nano-cage-filter-removes-98-percent-of-short-chain-pfas-from-tap-water-tackling-the-hardest-class-of-forever-chemicals) on a university-developed filtration technology targeting the same class of contaminants through a different mechanism.

## What We Don't Know

Neither source discloses Claros's post-money valuation, the exact split between new equity and the rolled-in convertible note, or a specific commercial timeline for the deployments across North America, Europe, and Asia that Tech Startups describes. It's also not clear from either source how many paying industrial or government customers Claros currently serves, or what the ClarosTechUV system costs to operate at scale relative to competing remediation methods.
